title: The Honest Continuity Hypothesis: ContinuousOn-Sphere Borsuk-Ulam and Ham Sandwich
description: Closes the loop left open by the parent entry. The parent (OQ-01-OQ-03-OQ-01) reduced the Ham Sandwich theorem to a single analytic input — continuity of the parameterized slice-volume map — and then PROVED in its Part 9 that this continuity is FALSE when read globally and only true on the sphere S^n, flagging 'reformulate the chain to ContinuousOn (Sphere n)' as the genuine remaining work. But the whole Borsuk-Ulam pipeline (SphereFun, no_continuous_odd_nonzero_on_sphere) is phrased with GLOBAL continuity, so the honest on-sphere hypothesis might not even be usable. This entry removes that worry: the radial extension sphereExtend h x = ||x|| . h(||x||^{-1} . x) turns any ContinuousOn (Sphere n) odd map into a globally continuous odd SphereFun that agrees with h on the sphere, so the global Borsuk-Ulam axiom IMPLIES the on-sphere antipodal collapse (borsuk_ulam_antipodal_collapse_on). Re-running the parent's reduction on top yields the entire Ham Sandwich chain with the continuity hypothesis stated exactly as Part 9 demanded — ContinuousOn (Sphere n) — culminating in ham_sandwich_standard_of_scalar_continuity_on. 11 theorems, 1 definition, 0 own axioms; rests on the inherited Borsuk-Ulam axiom (no_continuous_odd_nonzero_on_sphere) plus the stated on-sphere scalar continuity hypothesis.

The Ham Sandwich capstones additionally take the on-sphere continuity of the (scalar) slice-volume maps as a hypothesis (the residual Lebesgue-continuity input identified by the parent). The contribution is to prove the bridge from the GLOBAL Borsuk-Ulam axiom to the ON-SPHERE hypothesis (sphereExtend_continuous, borsuk_ulam_antipodal_collapse_on) and to re-derive the full Ham Sandwich chain under the honest ContinuousOn (Sphere n) hypothesis that the parent's Part 9 proved to be the faithful one.
originalContributions: sphereExtend: the radial extension of a map defined on the sphere, sphereExtend h x = ||x|| . h(||x||^{-1} . x) (and 0 at the origin), reusing only the values of h on S^n since the normalized argument always lies on the sphere
sphereExtend_eq_of_mem: the radial extension reproduces h on the sphere (where ||x|| = 1)
sphereExtend_odd: the radial extension is odd whenever h is — the scale ||x|| is even and ||x||^{-1} . (-x) = -(||x||^{-1} . x)

sphereExtend_continuous: THE CRUX — the radial extension is GLOBALLY continuous as soon as h is merely ContinuousOn (Sphere n). Off the origin it is a composition of continuous maps; at the origin continuity follows from the squeeze ||sphereExtend h x|| <= M . ||x|| with M an upper bound for ||h|| on the compact sphere (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn + squeeze_zero_norm)

borsuk_ulam_antipodal_collapse_on: the payoff — an odd map that is only ContinuousOn (Sphere n) still has a zero on the sphere, by feeding its radial extension (a genuine SphereFun) to the parent global antipodal collapse
borsuk_ulam_antipodal_collapse_of_sphereFun: the global SphereFun collapse is the special case of the on-sphere collapse, confirming the on-sphere statement is a strict generalization
ham_sandwich_reduction_on: the topological-core reduction (continuous-odd-with-bridge yields a bisecting point), now consuming ContinuousOn (Sphere n) instead of a global SphereFun

ham_sandwich_of_discrepancy_on: Ham Sandwich from a discrepancy map realized by a merely ContinuousOn (Sphere n) function; oddness via WithLp.ofLp_injective and discrepancy_odd_of_swap, zero-implies-bisected unchanged from the parent

ham_sandwich_of_scalar_continuity_on: the honest form of the parent's scalar-continuity Ham Sandwich — each of the 2n scalar slice-volume maps is assumed continuous ON S^n (where the map is genuinely continuous, the global version being provably false), assembled into a ContinuousOn (Sphere n) EuclideanSpace-valued discrepancy via (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n) R).symm

ham_sandwich_standard_of_scalar_continuity_on: the HEADLINE — Ham Sandwich for the standard linear cut whose only hypotheses are finite body volumes and on-sphere continuity of each scalar slice-volume, with the antipodal-swap and finiteness side conditions discharged from stdPos_neg, stdNeg_neg, volume_inter_ne_top. This is exactly the faithful hypothesis the parent's Part 9 identified, now shown sufficient to drive a full proof

overview.historicalContext: The Ham Sandwich theorem (Stone-Tukey, 1942) is the most famous corollary of the Borsuk-Ulam theorem (Borsuk, 1933), whose depth lies in degree theory for maps of spheres. The standard textbook derivation glosses over an analytic subtlety — continuity of the parameterized half-volume function — that a fully formal proof must isolate. The parent gallery entry isolated it exactly, and then discovered a sharp twist: for the standard linear cut, the half-volume map is NOT continuous globally (it jumps at the origin, where the cut degenerates to the empty half-space) but only continuous on the sphere. That left a structural gap, because the Borsuk-Ulam machinery in this project is phrased with global continuity. This entry settles the gap with a classical move from analysis — radial (positive-homogeneous degree-1) extension — showing the global topological input implies the honest on-sphere one at no extra cost.
overview.problemStatement: OQ-01-OQ-03-OQ-01-OQ-01: The parent file's Part 9 proved that the lone residual continuity hypothesis of the Ham Sandwich reduction must be read as ContinuousOn (Sphere n), not global Continuous, and flagged 'reformulate the chain to ContinuousOn throughout' as the genuine remaining work. But the underlying Borsuk-Ulam axiom and SphereFun structure demand GLOBAL continuity. Can the on-sphere hypothesis actually be used — i.e. does the global Borsuk-Ulam input imply the on-sphere antipodal collapse, and can the whole Ham Sandwich chain be re-derived under the honest ContinuousOn hypothesis?
overview.proofStrategy: Define the radial extension sphereExtend h x = ||x|| . h(||x||^{-1} . x). Prove it (1) agrees with h on the sphere, (2) is odd if h is, and (3) is globally continuous from ContinuousOn (Sphere n) h — off the origin by composition (the normalizing map into the sphere then h then scaling), at the origin by the squeeze ||sphereExtend h x|| <= M||x|| with M bounding ||h|| on the compact sphere. Feeding the extension (a SphereFun) to the parent borsuk_ulam_antipodal_collapse gives a zero on the sphere, which equals a zero of h there; this is borsuk_ulam_antipodal_collapse_on. Re-run the parent's Ham Sandwich reduction on top of the on-sphere collapse to obtain ham_sandwich_reduction_on, ham_sandwich_of_discrepancy_on, ham_sandwich_of_scalar_continuity_on, and the headline ham_sandwich_standard_of_scalar_continuity_on, all with ContinuousOn (Sphere n) continuity.
keyInsights: The global Borsuk-Ulam axiom IMPLIES its on-sphere refinement: any odd ContinuousOn (Sphere n) map extends radially to a globally continuous odd SphereFun agreeing with it on the sphere, so no strengthening of the axiom is needed.
Radial extension reuses only on-sphere values of h: the normalized argument ||x||^{-1} . x always lies on S^n, so h is never evaluated off the sphere where it might be wild.

The only nontrivial point of global continuity is at the origin, and it is handled by a uniform bound: h is bounded on the COMPACT sphere (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn), giving ||sphereExtend h x|| <= M||x|| -> 0 via squeeze_zero_norm.
Oddness of the extension is purely algebraic (||x|| even, ||x||^{-1}.(-x) = -(||x||^{-1}.x)), so it transfers the oddness of h with no analysis.

This makes the parent's Part 9 dichotomy airtight: the genuinely-remaining analytic input is the on-sphere Lebesgue continuity of a single real slice-volume, and EVERYTHING topological — including the bridge from the global axiom to the on-sphere hypothesis — is proved.

The on-sphere antipodal collapse strictly generalizes the global SphereFun one (borsuk_ulam_antipodal_collapse_of_sphereFun recovers the latter), so reformulating the chain to ContinuousOn loses nothing.

conclusion.summary: The parent entry isolated the lone analytic obstruction to a fully-formal Ham Sandwich theorem and then proved (Part 9) that this continuity is false read globally and only true on the sphere, leaving a structural worry: the entire Borsuk-Ulam pipeline is phrased with global continuity, so the honest on-sphere hypothesis might be unusable. This entry removes the worry. The radial extension sphereExtend turns any ContinuousOn (Sphere n) odd map into a globally continuous odd SphereFun agreeing with it on the sphere, so the global Borsuk-Ulam axiom implies the on-sphere antipodal collapse borsuk_ulam_antipodal_collapse_on. Re-running the parent's reduction yields the full Ham Sandwich chain with the continuity hypothesis stated exactly as Part 9 demanded — ContinuousOn (Sphere n) — culminating in ham_sandwich_standard_of_scalar_continuity_on, which proves simultaneous bisection of n bodies under the faithful hypothesis with all side conditions discharged.
conclusion.implications: The dichotomy opened by the parent is now airtight: the genuinely-remaining analytic input is the on-sphere Lebesgue continuity of a single real parameterized slice-volume, and everything topological — including the previously-missing bridge from the global axiom to the on-sphere hypothesis — is proved. The radial-extension technique is a reusable template: whenever a degree-theoretic existence result is packaged with global continuity but the natural hypothesis is only on-sphere (or on any star-shaped/compact base where positive-homogeneous extension applies), the global input can be upgraded to the on-sphere one for free. This also shows the on-sphere antipodal collapse strictly generalizes the SphereFun form, so the on-sphere reformulation of the whole chain loses nothing.
